text: Claims up to 25x faster installs than npm install
quote: ⚡️ 25x faster — Switch from `npm install` to `bun install` in any Node.js project to make your installations up to 25x faster.

text: Automatically migrates existing yarn.lock, package-lock.json, and pnpm-lock.yaml files when running bun install
quote: When you run `bun install` in a project without a `bun.lock`, Bun automatically migrates existing lockfiles: `yarn.lock` (v1), `package-lock.json` (npm...), `pnpm-lock.yaml` (pnpm)

text: Supports installing packages globally via -g/--global flag for CLI tools
quote: To install a package globally, use the `-g`/`--global` flag. Use it to install command-line tools.

text: Lets users explicitly allow lifecycle scripts for a package via trustedDependencies
quote: To tell Bun to allow lifecycle scripts for a particular package, add the package to `trustedDependencies` in your package.json.

text: Never touches the network for cached dependencies, erroring instead if a required package isn't cached
quote: Never touch the network (registry, tarball URLs, git); a required dependency that is not cached is an error

text: Runs a security audit by reading the lockfile and querying the npm advisory database
quote: Bun reads the package list from `bun.lock` (no `node_modules` required), sends it to the npm advisory endpoint, and prints a report.

text: Can automatically upgrade vulnerable packages to the lowest safe compatible version and reinstall
quote: Runs the audit, then upgrades each vulnerable package to the lowest non-vulnerable version that every dependent's range allows, and installs.

text: Supports workspaces to manage multiple independent packages in a single monorepo
quote: With workspaces, you develop several independent packages in a single repository, a _monorepo_.

text: Can filter installs to a subset of workspaces using the --filter flag
quote: In a monorepo, you can install the dependencies for a subset of packages using the `--filter` flag.

text: Can mark a workspace as self-contained so its dependencies aren't hoisted above it, keeping its node_modules complete
quote: Mark such a workspace as self-contained... For that workspace `bun install` then behaves as a hoisting barrier — nothing it depends on... is placed above `apps/desktop/node_modules`

text: Supports a shared dependency-version catalog referenced across workspaces via the catalog: protocol
quote: When many packages need the same dependency versions, define those versions once in a catalog in the root `package.json` and reference them from your workspaces with the `catalog:` protocol.

text: Maintains a global package cache to avoid re-downloading packages across projects
quote: Bun stores every package downloaded from the registry in a global cache at `~/.bun/install/cache`

text: Can list installed dependencies and their resolved versions
quote: To print a list of installed dependencies in the current project and their resolved versions, excluding their dependencies:

text: Can list installed packages grouped by license
quote: List every installed package grouped by license, as read from each package's `package.json` in `node_modules`.

text: Can show a diff of files and package.json changes between two versions of a package
quote: Show what changed between two versions of a package: a summary of the files and lines touched, the `package.json` changes worth a second look

text: Can pack a package into an npm-compatible .tgz archive
quote: `bun pm pack` creates a `.tgz` file containing all files that would be published to npm, following the same rules as `npm pack`.

text: Works as a drop-in package manager in any existing Node.js project that has a package.json
quote: It's a standalone tool that works in existing Node.js projects; if your project has a `package.json`, you can use `bun install`.

text: Supports npm's overrides and Yarn's resolutions fields for pinning transitive dependency versions
quote: Bun supports npm's `"overrides"` and Yarn's `"resolutions"` in `package.json`. Both specify a version range for _metadependencies_

text: Does not execute arbitrary lifecycle scripts like postinstall for dependencies by default, as a security measure
quote: Bun does not execute arbitrary lifecycle scripts like `postinstall` for installed dependencies. Executing arbitrary scripts represents a potential security risk.

text: Uses a human-readable, text-based bun.lock lockfile format
quote: Bun v1.2 changed the default lockfile format to the text-based `bun.lock`.

text: Uses hardlinks on Linux/Windows so package contents exist once on disk and are shared across projects
quote: On Linux and Windows, Bun uses hardlinks to "copy" a module into a project's `node_modules` directory, so the contents of the package only exist in a single location on disk.

text: Positions itself as a Node-compatible, dramatically faster drop-in replacement for npm, yarn, and pnpm
quote: The `bun` CLI contains a Node.js-compatible package manager designed to be a dramatically faster replacement for `npm`, `yarn`, and `pnpm`.

text: Supports a production install mode that skips devDependencies
quote: To install in production mode (without `devDependencies`):

text: Publishes measured benchmark numbers comparing install speed against npm
Provides bunx to execute a package's binary directly without a separate install step
quote: bunx cowsay 'Hello, world!'   # execute a package

text: Supports patching dependencies directly
quote: npm-compatible, up to 30× faster. Workspaces, catalogs, overrides, patches and a lockfile you can read.

text: --frozen-lockfile flag enforces installing exact lockfile versions without updating the lockfile
quote: For reproducible installs, use `--frozen-lockfile`. Bun installs the exact versions specified in the lockfile and does not update it.

text: bun install creates and maintains a bun.lock lockfile for reproducible dependency installs
quote: `bun install` creates a lockfile called `bun.lock`.
